messages:
Elena (Support): FYI escalation from Acme — their nightly long-running ingest job kept running across monthly boundary and then started getting 429s. Customer says tokens showed zero in UI for ~20m before refill. Asking for root cause and mitigation. attach: acme_trace_9042.zip
Acme App (customer): reproducer: longjob uploads ~4M tokens spanning 23:50->00:30 PST, at 00:00 we started seeing 429s and job failed. UI showed 0 credits for tenant for ~20 minutes, then at ~00:21 credits returned and job resumed. Can provide logs.
Elena (Support): thanks. Can you paste the exact curl you used and the 429 body if available?
Acme App (customer): here’s a snippet: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme" -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1000}'
```
Response: ```json
{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "monthly quota exhausted" }, "status": 429 }
```
Acme App (customer): trace-id: t1234-9042-00:07. We did not change plan. This was a continuous run from a single session.
Alex R (Support Eng): noted. Two immediate angles: 1) billing/topup pipeline (ledger -> tenant balance) 2) edge cache/UI TTL showing stale zero. Both can cause the symptom where API rejects but UI hasn't updated or vice-versa.
Elena (Support): @Priya can you check if tenant t-acme got ledger credits at midnight? Any scheduled jobs failed?
Priya (Billing): checking... I see the scheduled monthly credit job started at 23:59:50 UTC but one of the DB replicas was under maintenance and the job logged an error at 00:00:05 UTC. Retry kicked off at 00:19:40 UTC and completed at 00:20:15 UTC. Ledger shows credits applied at 00:20:15 UTC.
Elena (Support): ok that matches customer timeline — credits back at ~00:21. Why did API still return 429 between 00:00 and 00:20 if ledger was updated at 00:20?
Jon (SRE): likely cache propagation. Edge quota cache TTL is 60s but there's also a sticky in-memory node cache that can be longer if health probes show unhealthy DB. Let me pull edge logs for t-acme and trace-id.
Jon (SRE): pulled logs: trace t1234-9042 routed to edge node edge-17 at 00:06:03 PST. Edge-17 had cached tenant-balance = 0 with last refresh @ 23:58:30 PST. DB write at 00:20 didn't invalidate edge-17 until 00:20:40 (we push invalidation via pubsub but node's subscriber backlog prevented timely invalidation). So edge returned 429 based on stale cache.
Elena (Support): so root cause = billing job failed+retried, plus delayed pubsub propagation to some edge nodes. Two separate contributors.
Acme App (customer): is there anything we should change on our side? We run a single long session; is that a problem?
Alex R (Support Eng): long sessions can amplify the problem because they keep KV caches hot on single nodes and rely on propagation. Workarounds: 1) split into smaller jobs that check balance regularly and backoff gracefully 2) detect 429 monthly-quota and pause/retry with exponential backoff and a jitter + status check 3) ask us for Dedicated capacity if you need guaranteed uninterrupted throughput across monthly boundary.
Jon (SRE): short-term mitigation we applied: forced invalidation to edge-17 and bumped subscriber concurrency to drain backlog faster. Also added more verbose logging to the pubsub watchdog.
Priya (Billing): long-term we added a retry + alert on the scheduled credit job if the first run fails; also adjusting maintenance window scheduling to avoid conflict with monthly cutover for tenants with heavy longrunning jobs.
Elena (Support): Customer-facing summary for Acme: 
- What happened: midnight credit job initially failed due to DB replica maintenance; retry applied credits ~20m later. Meanwhile, some edge nodes had delayed pubsub invalidation and served cached zero-balance causing 429s.
- Impact: your long-running ingestion saw ~20m of 429s around the monthly boundary; UI showed zero during that window.
- Workarounds: split job / implement 429 retry with backoff / request Dedicated.
- What we did: forced edge invalidation, increased pubsub concurrency, added billing-job retry+alerts.
Acme App (customer): thanks. Can you provide repro steps for our engineers so we can test locally?
Alex R (Support Eng): repro steps: 1) create tenant on free tier with monthly bucket X 2) start a single long-running session that continuously sends tokens spanning the clock boundary 3) simulate delayed credit application by blocking the billing-write (or temporarily pause DB replica) at midnight 4) observe API 429 and UI zero for the window 5) run invalidation script to confirm edge recovers quickly.
Alex R (Support Eng): sample invalidation command we used (internal tool): ```bash
quota-invalidate --tenant t-acme --edge edge-17 --reason "missed-billing-retry"
```
Alex R (Support Eng): sample check for balance via API: ```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-admin" https://internal-api.redwood.ai/internal/tenants/t-acme/balance | jq .balance```
Jon (SRE): follow-up: we've also opened a ticket to detect tenants that run continuous long sessions across cutover and proactively pre-warm edge caches or place them on a short-window refresh during the transition.
Priya (Billing): closing loop: billing wrote credits at 00:20:15 UTC and invoice/ledger correct. We will reach out if we need customer approval to shift maintenance windows.
Elena (Support): marking this thread as actionable. @Acme App — we'll send a short postmortem + recommended code snippets. If you want, we can schedule a short call to walk through retries and Dedicated requirements. :calendar: :thumbsup: 
Acme App (customer): appreciated. Please include the exact timestamps and trace IDs. That helped us correlate logs.
Elena (Support): attaching timeline and traces to ticket TCK-8921. Closing thread here but will update when long-term pre-warm rollout hits canary. :eyes:
quota-bot: Notice: forced invalidation completed for edge-17 at 00:21:04 UTC (invalidate-id: inv-7789).
Jon (SRE): Postmortem note — root causes: (A) billing cutover job failed first-run due to replica maintenance; (B) pubsub subscriber backlog prevented timely invalidation to a subset of edges; contributing: single-node long session. Remediation: billing retry/alerts, increased subscriber concurrency, pre-warm for long sessions, recommend Dedicated for strict continuity.
Elena (Support): thanks team, marking resolved for now.
